title: Love One Another: The New Testament on Family Life
author: Mark D. Ellison
author_role: Associate Professor of Ancient Scripture, Brigham Young University

footnotes.text: This article draws from Mark D. Ellison, “Family, Marriage, and Celibacy in the New Testament,” inNew Testament History, Culture, and Society: A Background to the Texts of the New Testament, ed. Lincoln Blumell (2019), 532–54.

The verb translated “submit” or “subject” doesn’t appear in verse 22 but is borrowed from verse 21. The sense of the two verses is, “[21] Submit yourselves to each other, [22] wives to your husbands,” and so on through the household, with instructions specifying ways for each member to manifest thatmutualsubmission.

Slavery was a common practice in ancient societies and was not based on race or nationality. In the Roman Empire during New Testament times, many households had slaves, including Christian households. Slavery was not always lifelong. In our dispensation, the Lord declared that “it is not right that any man should be in bondage one to another” (Doctrine and Covenants 101:79).
